levels.title: Caching method results with pico-caching
levels.description: Memoise service methods through the container: TTL, custom keys, invalidation and the off switch.

levels.title: Your first @cacheable
levels.description:
Memoisation as a decorator

@cacheable stores what a method returns and serves the stored value on the next call with the same arguments. It works on sync and async methods alike; an async method caches the awaited result, never the coroutine.

Nothing is imported by the caller and nothing changes at the call site: the interceptor sits between them, so the method keeps its plain signature and stays testable on its own.

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

container = init(
    modules=[app],
    config=configuration(DictSource({"caching": {"enabled": True}})),
)

feed = container.get(app.PriceFeed)
print(feed.price("abc"), feed.price("abc"), feed.price("zz"))

assert feed.calls == 2, f"expected 2 upstream calls, got {feed.calls}"
print(f"three calls, {feed.calls} round trips")

hints: The decorator is already imported in app.py.
It works bare, without parentheses, when the defaults are fine.
@cacheable on the line above def price.

levels.title: Choosing the cache key
levels.description:
When the default key is too literal

By default the entry is keyed by the arguments as they arrive, so "eur" and "EUR" are two entries holding the same answer - the cache works, and still misses.

@cacheable(key=...) takes a callable that receives the method's arguments (without self) and returns the string to store under. Normalise there, and equivalent calls collapse into one entry.

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

container = init(
    modules=[app],
    config=configuration(DictSource({"caching": {"enabled": True}})),
)

quotes = container.get(app.Quotes)
print(quotes.rate("eur"), quotes.rate("EUR"), quotes.rate("Eur"))

assert quotes.calls == 1, f"expected one upstream call, got {quotes.calls}"
print("three spellings, one cache entry")

hints: @cacheable takes a key keyword argument: a callable returning the key.
It is called with the method arguments only - self is not passed to it.

levels.title: Invalidation
levels.description:
The hard part

A cache is a promise that the answer has not changed. When it has, someone must say so. CacheBackend is a component like any other, so you can resolve it and act on the store directly: get, set, delete and clear.

The default implementation is InMemoryCacheBackend, bounded by caching.max_entries. Swapping it for a shared store is a matter of registering your own component that satisfies the same protocol.

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
from pico_caching import CacheBackend
import app

container = init(
    modules=[app],
    config=configuration(DictSource({"caching": {"enabled": True}})),
)

catalog = container.get(app.Catalog)
first = catalog.name("x")
assert catalog.name("x") == first, "the second read should be served from cache"

# The product was renamed upstream. The cache does not know that.
# TODO: drop what is cached so the next read goes to the source again.

second = catalog.name("x")
assert second != first, f"still serving the stale value: {second}"
print(f"{first} -> {second}")
print("invalidated, and only then did the source get asked again")

solution.main.py:
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
from pico_caching import CacheBackend
import app

container = init(
    modules=[app],
    config=configuration(DictSource({"caching": {"enabled": True}})),
)

catalog = container.get(app.Catalog)
first = catalog.name("x")
assert catalog.name("x") == first, "the second read should be served from cache"

# The product was renamed upstream. The cache does not know that.
container.get(CacheBackend).clear()

second = catalog.name("x")
assert second != first, f"still serving the stale value: {second}"
print(f"{first} -> {second}")
print("invalidated, and only then did the source get asked again")

hints: CacheBackend is registered in the container; resolve it like any component.
Its interface is get, set, delete and clear.

levels.title: Turning it off from configuration
levels.description:
An operational switch, not a code change

CacheSettings binds the caching prefix: enabled, default_ttl_seconds (300 by default) and max_entries (1024). With enabled false the interceptor steps aside and every call reaches the method, decorators untouched.

That is what you want in a test suite, and what you want in production the day the cache is serving something it should not - together with POST /actuator/refresh it flips without a restart.

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

# A test run wants the real method every time, not yesterday's answer.
# TODO: switch caching off from configuration, without touching app.py.
CONFIG = {"caching": {"enabled": True}}

container = init(modules=[app], config=configuration(DictSource(CONFIG)))

report = container.get(app.Report)
report.total()
report.total()

assert report.calls == 2, f"caching still on: {report.calls} call(s)"
print(f"two calls, {report.calls} executions - the decorator stayed in place")

solution.main.py:
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

# A test run wants the real method every time, not yesterday's answer.
CONFIG = {"caching": {"enabled": False}}

container = init(modules=[app], config=configuration(DictSource(CONFIG)))

report = container.get(app.Report)
report.total()
report.total()

assert report.calls == 2, f"caching still on: {report.calls} call(s)"
print(f"two calls, {report.calls} executions - the decorator stayed in place")

hints: The setting lives under the caching prefix in the config source.
You do not need to remove the decorator; the interceptor reads the setting.
